experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for the preparation of indole derivatives: In a typical experiment, 1.5 g of L-(+)-tartaric acid-DMU (30:70) mixture was heated to 70 °C to obtain a clear melt. To this melt, 1 mmol of aryl hydrazine.HCl and 1 mmol of aldehyde/ketone were added at 70 °C. The reaction was monitored by thin layer chromatography. After completion, the reaction mixture was quenched by adding water while still hot. The reaction mixture was cooled to room temperature and the solid that separated was filtered and washed with water (2 x 5 mL). The crude compound was dried under vacuum and recrystallized from ethanol to afford pure product. In case of liquid products, the reaction mixture was quenched with water and the aqueous layer was extracted with DCM (3 x 5 mL). The organic layer was washed with water (2 x 5 mL), dried over anhydrous Na2SO4 and concentrated under reduced pressure. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: (13) Typical procedures for synthesis of 3a-d and 4a-d in method 3 performing the Fischer indolization: Ketone 5a or 5b-d (1 mmol) was refluxed in ethanol with phenylhydrazine (1.1 mmol) and acetic acid (0.2 mmol) or with p-methoxyphenylhydrazine hydrochloride (1.1 mmol) for 0.5 h (TLC monitoring). title: A convenient modification of the Fischer indole synthesis with a solid acid
authors: Chandrasekhar, Sosale; Mukherjee, Somnath
reference: A convenient modification of the Fischer indole synthesis with a solid acid | Chandrasekhar, Sosale; Mukherjee, Somnath | Synthetic Communications (2015), 45(8), 1018-1022
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: EXPERIMENTAL A mixture of the carbonyl compound (5, 1.0mmol), arylhydrazine (6, 1.2mmol), and the solid acid (7, Amberlite, 1.5g, obtained from Aldrich Chemical Co.) was refluxed in absolute ethanol (10ml) for 8h. The reaction was monitored by thin-layer chromatography (TLC), and upon completion the mixture was cooled to room temperature, the catalyst filtered off, and and the product was washed thoroughly with ethyl acetate (30ml). The combined organics were washed with water, dried (Na2SO4), and concentrated in vacuo. The resulting residue was chromatographed on a silica gel column eluting with ethyl acetate-hexane mixtures. The purified indole (8). This was fully characterized by infrared, 400-MHz 1H NMR, high-resolution mass spectrometry, and melting point (solids). 10 6-Methoxy-2,3,4,9-tetrahydro-1-H-carbazole. purified on silica gel 100-200 mesh (EtOAc/Hexane 10/90); yellow solid, yield 85%. TLC Rf 0.40 (20% EtOAc/Hexane); mp 108-110°C (lit.2 110-112°C); ν max 3392, 2910, 1583, 1480, 1210, 1025; δH 7.69 (brs, 1H), 7.15-7.13 (d, 1H, J 8 Hz), 6.93-6.92 (d, 1H, J J 2 Hz), 6.77-6.74 (m, 1H), 3.85 (s, 3H), 2.70-2.66 (m, 4H0, 1.89-1.86 (m, 4H); δC 153.6, 134.9, 130.6, 128.0, 110.8, 110.3, 109.8, 108.8, 100.1, 55.8, 23.1, 23.0, 20.8; m/z calcd. for M+H 202.1148, found 202.1139.

title: Chloroaluminate ionic liquid for Fischer indole synthesis
authors: Rebeiro, Geeta L.; Khadilkar, Bhushan M.
reference: Chloroaluminate ionic liquid for Fischer indole synthesis | Rebeiro, Geeta L.; Khadilkar, Bhushan M. | Synthesis (2001), (3), 370-372
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Chloroaluminate Ionic Liquid17 Freshly sublimed AlCl3 (134 g, 1 mol) was added to n-BuPyCl (50 g, 0.5 mol) at r.t. under N2 to give the chloroaluminate ionic liquid. Cyclization of Arylhydrazones of Ketones 1-11 Using Ionic Liquid; 2-Phenyl-3-methylindole (3); Typical Procedure A mixture of phenylhydrazine (0.9 g, 8.3 mmol) and propiophenone (1.1 g, 8.3 mmol) was added dropwise to ionic liquid (1.5 mL, 6.5 mmol), at 180-185 °C for 3 h under efficient stirring under N2. After the reaction was complete (monitored by TLC), it was quenched with H2O/concd HCl, extracted with Et2O, and the Et2O solution was passed through anhyd Na2SO4. The Et2O was removed to obtain the desired product, which was purified either by recrystallization (EtOH) or by silica gel column chromatography using petroleum ether (bp 60-80 °C)/EtOAc (99:1) mixture as the eluent. 1,2,3,4-tetrahydro-6-methylcarbazole, yield 90%. Mp found: 138 °C; reported: 141-142 °C.

title: A convenient modification of the Fischer indole synthesis with a solid acid
authors: Chandrasekhar, Sosale; Mukherjee, Somnath
reference: A convenient modification of the Fischer indole synthesis with a solid acid | Chandrasekhar, Sosale; Mukherjee, Somnath | Synthetic Communications (2015), 45(8), 1018-1022
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: EXPERIMENTAL A mixture of the carbonyl compound (5, 1.0mmol), arylhydrazine (6, 1.2mmol), and the solid acid (7, Amberlite, 1.5g, obtained from Aldrich Chemical Co.) was refluxed in absolute ethanol (10ml) for 8h. The reaction was monitored by thin-layer chromatography (TLC), and upon completion the mixture was cooled to room temperature, the catalyst filtered off, and and the product was washed thoroughly with ethyl acetate (30ml). The combined organics were washed with water, dried (Na2SO4), and concentrated in vacuo. The resulting residue was chromatographed on a silica gel column eluting with ethyl acetate-hexane mixtures. The purified indole (8). This was fully characterized by infrared, 400-MHz 1H NMR, high-resolution mass spectrometry, and melting point (solids). 8 1,2,3,4-Tetrahydrocyclopenta[b]indole. purified on silica gel 100-200 mesh (EtOAc/Hexane 10/90); white solid, yield 84%. reference: Evaluation of a Nonresonant Microwave Applicator for Continuous-Flow Chemistry Applications | Oehrngren, Per; Fardost, Ashkan; Russo, Francesco; Schanche, Jon-Sverre; Fagrell, Magnus; Larhed, Mats | Organic Process Research & Development (2012), 16(5), 1053-1063
experimental_procedure: 2,3,4,9-Tetrahydro-1H-carbazole (11). Two stock solutions were prepared: a hydrazine solution of phenylhydrazine (9) (30 mmol) diluted to 30 mL in acetic acid/2-propanol (3:1) and a ketone solution of cyclohexanone (10) (33 mmol) diluted to 30 mL in acetic acid/2-propanol (3:1). The two solutions were connected to each pump channel and pumped through the CF-MAOS system with residence times and temperatures between 20-300 s and 210-230 °C, respectively, for optimization purposes. A reaction mixture of 30 mL was collected over 14 min with a residence time of 20 s at 230 °C (10 mL pump-1 min-1) to determine the isolated yield for the optimized reaction conditions. The reaction mixture was cooled down to room temperature and poured into 100 mL of ice-water under magnetic stirring which produced a pale-yellow/creamy precipitate. Stirring continued until all of the ice had melted, after which the suspension was filtrated and the precipitate washed with cold water. The washed precipitate was dried under reduced pressure overnight. Yield: 13.4 mmol (2.3 g). Pale, cream-colored solid in 90% isolated yield with an estimated throughput of 57.2 mmol/h (9.8 g/h). 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3) δ 7.64 (br. s., 1H), 7.48 (dt, J = 7.5, 0.8 Hz, 1H), 7.28 (dq, J = 7.6, 0.7 Hz, 1H), 7.16-7.06 (m, 2H), 2.77-2.70 (m, 4H), 1.99-1.85 (m, 4H). 13C NMR (101 MHz, CDCl3) δ 135.8, 134.2, 127.9, 121.1, 119.2, 117.9, 110.4, 110.3, 23.4, 23.4, 23.4, 21.0; LC-MS m/z: 172 [M + H]+. Mp: 115-117 °C (lit. 115-116 °C).

title: Fischer Indole Synthesis in Low Melting Mixtures

reference: Fischer Indole Synthesis in Low Melting Mixtures | Gore, Sangram; Baskaran, Sundarababu; Koenig, Burkhard | Organic Letters (2012), 14(17), 4568-4571
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for the preparation of indole derivatives: In a typical experiment, 1.5 g of L-(+)-tartaric acid-DMU (30:70) mixture was heated to 70 °C to obtain a clear melt. To this melt, 1 mmol of aryl hydrazine.HCl and 1 mmol of aldehyde/ketone were added at 70 °C. The reaction was monitored by thin layer chromatography. After completion, the reaction mixture was quenched by adding water while still hot. The reaction mixture was cooled to room temperature and the solid that separated was filtered and washed with water (2 x 5 mL). The crude compound was dried under vacuum and recrystallized from ethanol to afford pure product. In case of liquid products, the reaction mixture was quenched with water and the aqueous layer was extracted with DCM (3 x 5 mL). The organic layer was washed with water (2 x 5 mL), dried over anhydrous Na2SO4 and concentrated under reduced pressure. The crude compound was purified by column chromatography over silica gel. 3c. 6,7,8,9,10,11-Hexahydro-5H-cycloocta[b]indole, colorless solid, yield 96%.
